AlphaGov delivers public-sector consulting for cities, counties, school systems, special districts, utilities, and related agencies. Our work spans classification and compensation, organizational and operational studies, research and program evaluation, economic and workforce analysis, surveys and community research, and applied data and infrastructure research.

We engage experienced practitioners as project-based collaborators. Engagements are remote-first with occasional client travel. When you authorize it, AlphaGov may name you as an expert collaborator or key personnel on proposals that match your expertise. We build ready teams for live pursuits — not speculative staffing banks.

AlphaGov is engaging an EV Charging Infrastructure Engineer for current public-sector EV charging studies and site design reviews. You will analyze electrical capacity, charger siting, make-ready needs, and interconnection constraints so agencies can build reliable Level 2 and DC fast-charging infrastructure.

We confirm scope, schedule, and fee with you before any engagement begins.

What you'll do

  • Review site electrical capacity, panel schedules, transformers, and service upgrades for charger loads
  • Produce or review EVSE layouts, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and make-ready scopes
  • Coordinate utility service planning, interconnection applications, and meter or rate options
  • Advise on Level 2 and DCFC hardware selection, power sharing, and code compliance (NEC, local AHJ)
  • Support cost estimates for electrical upgrades, trenching, and charger installation packages
  • Flag constructability, safety, and accessibility issues before agencies bid or award install work
  • Contribute qualifications and past-performance narrative to AlphaGov proposals when you authorize naming

Apply to be considered.

Requirements

Required

  • Professional experience designing or reviewing EV charging electrical infrastructure for agencies or commercial sites
  • Working knowledge of Level 2 and DC fast charging, load calculations, and utility make-ready requirements
  • Ability to interpret single-line diagrams and produce engineer-ready findings an agency can act on
  • Comfortable as a 1099 project-based consultant, remote-first with occasional site visits

Nice to have

  • Licensed Professional Engineer (PE) in electrical or a closely related discipline
  • Experience with municipal, county, transit depot, or highway corridor charging projects
  • Familiarity with NEVI, CFI, or state EVSE design and compliance standards

About Us

Highland Electric Fleets’ mission is to make electric fleets accessible and affordable for all, enabling communities to realize the benefits of cleaner, quieter and healthier fleets. Highland is North America’s leading provider of Electrification-as-a-Service (EaaS). Founded in 2019, Highland partners with school districts, municipalities, and fleet operators to make the transition to electric fleets simple and affordable.
Highland proudly serves as the Official Electric School Bus Provider of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Team USA. From pioneering vehicle-to-grid technology to managing some of the nation’s largest electric school bus fleets, Highland delivers reliable, cost-effective solutions that support local communities and drive the future of transportation.

Summary:

The Project Engineer owns the engineering design packages that take qualified sites through to permit-ready status across a large, fast-moving portfolio of EV charging, battery energy storage (BESS), and edge compute projects.

Reporting to the Engineering Manager, the Project Engineer generates and reviews conceptual-through-construction design packages, functionally leads Highland's external engineering partners, and serves as the technical authority on utility and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements — carrying the 30%, Issued-for-Permit (IFP), and permit-application packages that bring each site to build-ready.

Responsibilities:

  • Generate project-specific conceptual and schematic design packages.
  • Review and approve project-specific conceptual, schematic, development, permit, and
    construction design packages.
  • Solicit and respond to project-specific design inquiries from customers, consultants, contractors,
    utilities, and permitting authorities.
  • Direct and quality-check the work of external engineering partners (e.g., NV5) to keep design
    packages moving on an aggressive, portfolio-wide timeline.
  • Ensure adherence to engineering and design specifications and best practices.
  • Ensure adherence to Highland engineering package content and structure.
  • Interpret utility and AHJ technical requirements and ensure compliant designs.
  • Support development of a repository for utility and AHJ design requirements.
  • Support the evaluation and selection of contractor proposals.

Qualifications:

    Required
  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, or 8+ years of directly related professional
    experience.
  • 3–5+ years of experience in project-based design management (renewable energy, EV
    charging infrastructure, or power grids desirable).
  • 2+ years of construction project design specification development and management.
  • 3+ years of managing third-party engineering consultants.
  • 3+ years of creating, editing, and commenting in CAD tools, with expertise in AutoCAD.
    Preferred
  • 1+ years of EV charging infrastructure project design experience.
  • Familiarity with project management and review software (Procore, Bluebeam).

What You Can Expect from Highland:

  • Competitive base salary and performance-based bonus program
  • A supportive, highly collaborative, team-oriented environment
  • Ability to work with bright, innovative, and forward-thinking colleagues
  • Health, Vision, and Dental coverage for employees & their dependents
  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • 401(k) program and company match

it's electric is a curbside electric vehicle charging company with deployments underway in 11 US cities. it’s electric provides a public charging solution that addresses the infrastructural barriers cities face in the deployment of electric vehicle charging. Applicants should be excited to do the work with one of the fastest growing climate and transportation start-ups in the country.

📣 Calling all Philadelphia-based Professional Engineers looking to pivot into Climate & Energy 📣

Role Description:

The Project Engineer role centers on strategically deploying it’s electric’s unique model of curbside charging infrastructure in Philadelphia.

Responsibilities include:

  • Overall project management for charger deployments
  • Site assessment and evaluation, including available power capacity
  • Overall project design and engineering, including drawings and specifications
  • Signing and stamping permit drawings to local authorities
  • Coordination with local permit authorities and utilities

• Contractor bid and award

  • Construction administration and coordination
  • Evolving and expanding company-wide technical and strategic standards
  • Evaluation of alternative and novel means and methods that reduce charger installation cost and time
  • Management of technical sub-consultants
  • Coordination with it’s electric project managers and designers across regions
  • Representation of it’s electric at property site visits, public hearings, and community board events.

Requirements

Candidate Requirements:

We seek highly motivated candidates with 5 to 10 years of experience in electrical engineering. Candidates should have examples of complex urban design and build projects (extra points if in urban rights-of-way) that have been physically built and are in use. Experience deploying EV charging is not a requirement; however, all candidates should be knowledgeable about electrical distribution systems in cities and buildings. Candidates should be familiar with and comfortable interpreting NFPA 70 (NEC) and the National Electric Safety Code.

Strong candidates will have experience seeing complex projects through from concept to completion. Candidates should be comfortable using traditional collaborative drafting and diagramming tools (AutoCAD, Bluebeam) and be able to clearly convey engineering principles using non-technical language. Candidates will have experience working with trades and contractors during the construction and sign-off phases, and will be able to contribute to the development and ongoing maintenance of project tracking and documentation tools and assets.

As this is a fully remote role, candidates are expected to be highly autonomous, comfortable with occasional ambiguity, able to manage time effectively, and effective communicators (erring on the side of over-communication). Candidates should demonstrate the ability to thrive without direct daily supervision, and be highly organized to independently advance projects. As such, the engineer will make engineering calculations to prepare engineering designs and specifications; prepare plans and drawings neatly and accurately to it’s electric’s guidelines; deal effectively with contractors, property owners and the general public; understand and interpret engineering as-builts; and ensure project compliance with State, Federal, and local rules, laws and regulations, including as set by the local utility.

it’s electric is a rapidly growing start-up, and we are looking for candidates willing to embrace the challenges and excitement inherent in a growing company. The role will challenge candidates to work with new technology, develop novel processes, and implement standard procedures that develop over time. Candidates must demonstrate the capacity to build and maintain productive, positive, and long-term relationships with stakeholders, while proactively and assertively tending the permitting, technical, and highly targeted project schedule.

Only Licensed Professional Engineers, or engineers who have completed their Engineer-in-Training programs will be considered for this role. Licensed PE is strongly preferred. Professional license must be maintained as a condition of employment.

Physical Requirements:

Candidates must be able to lift equipment (up to 40 pounds) as necessary. This position is fully remote; however, candidates should have flexibility to travel for local meetings in person as needed, as well as to it’s electric’s headquarters in Brooklyn (also as needed).

The salary range for this role is $150K-$160K, depending on length and relevance of candidate’s experience.

Medical / Dental / Vision

18 Days PTO

11 Holidays

Hybrid Schedule

Company Equity

Role Summary

The Business Development Manager, Distributed Energy, is responsible for accelerating Fluke’s penetration and market share across the rapidly expanding EV charging infrastructure and solar/energy-storage ecosystems. This role blends strategic market development with hands-on selling to unlock new logo wins, drive product-line expansion, secure multi-site contracts, and influence standards and specifications that preference Fluke test and measurement tools.

The role spans the full distributed energy value chain: EV charge point operators (CPOs) and network providers, EVSE installers and electrical contractors, fleet electrification programs, solar EPCs, O&M providers, utility-scale solar and storage owner-operators, commissioning agents, and utilities interconnecting distributed energy resources. A strong understanding of EVSE installation and maintenance workflows, PV system commissioning and O&M, energy storage, and electrical safety practices is essential.

Key Responsibilities

Market Expansion & Business Development

  • Build and execute a strategic growth plan to expand Fluke’s presence across EV charging (public DCFC networks, fleet depots, workplace/retail L2) and solar (utility-scale, C&I, and distributed PV plus storage).
  • Identify and convert new logo opportunities across CPOs, EVSE manufacturers and installers, fleet operators, solar EPCs, O&M providers, asset owners, commissioning agents, and utilities supporting DER interconnection.
  • Develop multi-year growth strategies for key distributed energy customers and map executive stakeholders and influencers to secure enterprise-wide adoption, specification preference, and expansion opportunities.
  • Develop standardized Fluke-preferred workflows and playbooks for EVSE commissioning and maintenance technicians, PV installers, O&M field teams, and electrical contractors.
  • Drive adoption of Fluke solutions across installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and electrical safety workflows.
  • Analyze competitive solutions and market dynamics to develop strategies that position Fluke as the preferred test and measurement provider across distributed energy workflows.

Pipeline Creation & Conversion

  • Establish and execute a 12–24-month pipeline focused on critical product categories including EV charging station analyzers, solar irradiance and I-V curve tracing tools, insulation testers, CAT III 1500 V solar instruments, power quality analyzers, thermal imaging, battery analyzers, and digital multimeters.
  • Generate early-stage funnel through proactive outreach to CPOs, EVSE installers, solar EPCs, O&M providers, and utility DER programs.
  • Drive demand through vertical events, industry associations (e.g., RE+, SEIA, CharIN, EVSE/NECA forums), and strategic channel activation.
  • Co-sell with field sellers and channel partners to progress high-value deals through close.
  • Own revenue growth, pipeline development, and market-share expansion objectives for the distributed energy segment, with accountability for converting strategic opportunities into scalable, multi-site customer relationships.

Contracts, Standards, and Specifications

  • Influence standards and specifications at CPOs, EPCs, asset owners, and utilities to require Fluke tools across EVSE commissioning, PV acceptance testing (IEC 62446), storage, and electrical safety workflows.
  • Secure multi-site and multi-year agreements that consolidate spend and reduce TCO for network operators, EPCs, and O&M providers.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with Marketing and Product Management to identify key distributed energy customer personas, define their operational workflows and pain points, and translate those insights into targeted messaging, solution positioning, and market development strategies.
  • Partner with Marketing to develop verticalized content, case studies, and campaigns tailored to EV charging and solar audiences.
  • Provide VOC to Product Management to inform roadmap prioritization for EVSE, PV, and energy-storage test needs.
  • Support Sales Enablement in building segment-specific training for field sellers, distributors, and contractor-focused teams.

Thought Leadership & Vertical Expertise

  • Serve as Fluke’s subject matter expert across the distributed energy ecosystem including EV charging networks, fleet electrification, solar EPC/O&M, and energy storage.
  • Articulate Fluke's value proposition around productivity, reliability, safety, regulatory compliance, and total cost of ownership during executive-level customer engagements and industry forums.
  • Represent Fluke at conferences, commissioning groups, contractor forums, and technical associations tied to e-mobility and renewable energy.
  • Educate internal teams on emerging trends such as NEVI/state charging programs, high-power charging, megawatt charging for fleets, solar-plus-storage growth, interconnection constraints, and evolving codes and standards (NEC, UL, IEC).

Qualifications

  • 8–12+ years of experience in business development, strategic sales, or key account management within distributed energy, EV infrastructure, solar, energy storage, electrical infrastructure, test & measurement, or related technical industries.
  • Demonstrated success driving new logo acquisition, account expansion, and multi-site or multi-year agreements in complex B2B environments.
  • Strong understanding of distributed energy ecosystems, including EV charging infrastructure, solar generation, energy storage, utilities, fleet electrification, and contractor networks.
  • Working knowledge of EVSE installation and maintenance workflows, PV commissioning processes, energy storage systems, electrical safety practices, and applicable industry codes and standards.
  • Experience engaging with and selling to charge point operators (CPOs), EVSE manufacturers and installers, solar EPCs, O&M providers, utilities, fleet operators, asset owners, commissioning agents, or related stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to build and execute strategic account plans, map stakeholders, and influence decision-makers at multiple organizational levels, including executive leadership.
  • Experience developing and managing 12–24 month pipelines, including early-stage opportunity creation and funnel development.
  • Ability to articulate value propositions tied to reliability, safety, productivity, regulatory compliance, and total cost of ownership (TCO).
  • Track record of cross-functional collaboration with sales, marketing, product management, and channel partners to drive revenue outcomes.
  • Strong executive communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.
  • Experience selling through and with distribution channel partners.
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% across North America.
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

  • Direct experience in EV charging infrastructure, solar construction and commissioning, energy storage systems, distributed energy resources (DERs), or electrical infrastructure environments.
  • Background selling or supporting test and measurement equipment, power quality tools, thermal imaging, electrical safety instrumentation, battery analysis, or related technologies.
  • Experience influencing standards, specifications, or approved vendor lists within large operators, EPCs, utilities, fleet organizations, or asset owners.
  • Familiarity with distributed energy technologies and emerging trends, including high-power EV charging, fleet electrification, solar-plus-storage systems, DER interconnection, and grid modernization initiatives.
  • Experience working with or selling through channel partners, distributors, contractor networks, or utility ecosystems.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop vertical-specific workflows, playbooks, or standardized solutions.
  • Knowledge of industry standards and regulatory frameworks impacting EV charging, solar, energy storage, electrical safety, and compliance.
  • Experience participating in or presenting at industry associations, technical forums, standards organizations, or conferences.
  • Ability to analyze competitive landscapes and develop displacement strategies.
  • Master of Business Administration (MBA) or advanced degree preferred.

Through our Charging-as-a-Service (CaaS) business, we are moving up the stack beyond hardware to enable large enterprises to own and operate branded EV fast charging networks without the hassle.

CaaS is not a traditional CPO model.

We provide supermarket and discount chains, fuel and convenience retailers, QSR brands and large landowners with a fully integrated, white-label platform that combines:

  • ABB’s industry-leading DC charging hardware

  • Asset management with contractual uptime guarantees

  • End-to-end business operations

  • Frontend driver services

Our partners retain control of their brand, pricing and customer relationship while we handle the technical and operational complexity.

Our ambition in DACH is to make CaaS the preferred charging platform partner for enterprise portfolios across Germany, Switzerland and Austria.

The Partnership Development Lead, DACH owns CaaS revenue and order intake in Germany, Switzerland and Austria. You own the pipeline, the number and the partner relationships behind it.

This is a founding commercial role. You will be our first CaaS hire in the region, taking the business from the first deals and conversations to a portfolio of multi-site partners across three countries. You personally hunt, close and lead the enterprise partnerships that define our position in the market.

You will report to the Global Head of Charging-as-a-Service and work day to day with our European operations, strategy and product teams. Your job is to win the partners that put CaaS on the map in your region.

  • Own the CaaS revenue and order intake target for DACH and the account plan to deliver it

  • Build a partnership ecosystem across site design, engineering, civil works, electrical installation so projects get delivered on time

  • Represent ABB E-mobility and CaaS at industry events in the region

  • Stay the commercial owner of signed partners as our operations team takes over delivery and day-to-day service

  • Bring DACH market and regulatory requirements into the CaaS product and technology roadmap

Ideal candidate profile

We are looking for someone who enjoys winning new business and building something from the ground up. You likely bring:

  • 7+ years in consulting or business development

  • Expertise selling technical products or solutions to enterprise customers

  • Owner mentality. Hands-on and self-starting, willing to roll up the sleeves to get a result

  • Comfort operating with high autonomy inside a global corporation, and the judgment to know when to draw on the ABB organization and when to move independently

  • Fluent German and English

Location

Germany, with scope across Germany, Switzerland and Austria. Remote-first, with regular travel to partner and customer sites, ABB E-mobility locations in the region, and our European office.
